doc.title: Eddie Marshall interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Max Roach practicing at his house
summary: Max Roach visited his house, played drums for half an hour and fell asleep in the garden; Marshall calls him his hero.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Really. He’s getting pretty frail now but he’s still — so I left him there playing, he’s practicing on the drums. And I said, “Well Max I have to step out for a minute.” So actually I just stepped out in the kitchen. And so he’s playing. And he’s just playing this stuff it’s like — like when I’m practicing I’m always going [steady scat]. And he’s going [rhythmic scat] he’s playing all this stuff and it’s like a half hour he’s playing. So I left. Because he was just into it. And I came back and he was still playing. And then I come back and he says, “Oh man these drums sound great.” And I said. “Well Max, why don’t you come and sit in the back yard.” I have a garden in the back you know. So I brought him in the back and the sun is shining and he lays back and he just fell dead asleep. And it was so nice to have this guy that’s my hero.
Did you tell him about the little thing?
No I never didn’t. I hope I’ll see him again. He’s a marvelous person.
